body:
Found while writing user-facing copy telling people to sync after a repair. The
copy could not be justified, and the reason it could not is the finding.

## What the repair actually does

`cps/tasks/kepub_package_repair.py:332` marks the book:

    helper.mark_book_modified(candidate, set_dirty=False, unsync=False)

`cps/helper.py:75` stamps `book.last_modified` and, ONLY when `unsync=True`,
calls `kobo_sync_status.remove_synced_book(book.id, all=True)` — which its own
docstring describes as the step that makes "every device re-pull". The repair
task passes `unsync=False`, so that step never runs.

## What the device receives

OBSERVED, `cps/kobo.py:1053` `create_book_entitlement`:

    "CrossRevisionId": book_uuid,
    "Id":              book_uuid,
    "RevisionId":      book_uuid,
    "Created":         book.timestamp,
    "LastModified":    book.last_modified,     <- the only field the repair changes

The repair rewrites bytes on disk. It does not change the book's UUID or its
`timestamp`. So the entitlement the device gets carries **the same revision
identity it already holds**, with a newer LastModified.

OBSERVED, `cps/kobo.py:655-660` + `get_kobo_created_ts` (`kobo.py:140`): the
NewEntitlement/ChangedEntitlement choice is `ts_created > sync_token.books_last_created`,
where `ts_created` comes from `Books.timestamp` / `date_added` — never from
`KoboSyncedBooks`. Once a device has synced a book, its cursor is past that
book's creation timestamp forever, so a repaired book emits **ChangedEntitlement
on every subsequent sync, unconditionally**.

## The part that is documented wrong, twice

Two places state that clearing `KoboSyncedBooks` is what produces a
NewEntitlement:

- `cps/admin.py:1445` — "Clears the (user_id, book_id) row from
  kobo_synced_books so the sync emits NewEntitlement"
- `tests/unit/test_kobo_admin_resend_book.py:81` — "without the deletion the
  next sync emits ChangedEntitlement rather than re-delivering the file"

The second is a SOURCE-PINNED test, so it asserts the string is present in
`do_kobo_resend` and never executes the claim. Per `get_kobo_created_ts`,
deleting that row cannot change the entitlement type — the type is decided
entirely by timestamps. Whatever makes `do_kobo_resend` work, the stated
mechanism is not it.

That matters beyond tidiness: this belief is what anyone would rely on to decide
whether the repair reaches devices, and it is load-bearing in exactly the place
nothing verifies it.

## What is genuinely unknown

UNOBSERVED: whether a Kobo re-downloads a book's file when it receives a
ChangedEntitlement whose RevisionId it already has. Nobody has measured it. The
repository's own comments assert it does not, but on a mechanism that does not
exist, so those comments are not evidence.

If it does not re-download, then **the KEPUB repair task has no effect on any
device that already has the book** — i.e. no effect on precisely the population
it exists to help, since a book has to have been synced to be broken on a device.

## The experiment that settles it

Cheap, and safe if scoped to a disposable book:
1. Pick a book already synced to the device that carries NO annotations.
2. Record the on-device file's size/mtime/hash.
3. Rewrite it server-side and bump `last_modified` only (exactly what the repair
   does — do NOT clear KoboSyncedBooks).
4. Sync. Re-measure the on-device file.
Changed bytes => ChangedEntitlement re-delivers and the repair works as intended.
Unchanged => the repair is invisible to already-synced devices and needs
`unsync=True` (or another delivery mechanism) to do anything at all.

Run the same experiment a second time WITH the synced row cleared, to find out
what `do_kobo_resend` is actually relying on.

## Do not "fix" this by flipping unsync=True until that is measured

Forcing re-delivery of every repaired book is not obviously safe: re-delivery
changes spine filenames for split/normalized packages, and the device's existing
Bookmark rows are matched by ContentID. A forced redownload could strand
highlights that currently still render. Measure first.

--- SCOPE CORRECTION, 2026-08-19: the belief is load-bearing TWICE, in opposite
--- directions, and neither use verified it ---

I filed this as "the repair may never reach a device". Searching the repository's
own notes for prior hardware work turned up notes/3649-kobo-format-change-
entitlement-design.md, which rests on the SAME unverified premise for the
opposite purpose:

  line 69: metadata edits "legitimately need ChangedEntitlement so the Kobo
           updates metadata IN PLACE WITHOUT RE-DOWNLOADING"
  line 72: an always-NewEntitlement patch would mean "the Kobo re-downloads
           content it already has, and on some firmware creates a duplicate
           library entry"

So:

  * cps/admin.py + test_kobo_admin_resend_book.py treated "ChangedEntitlement
    does not re-deliver" as a PROBLEM to work around;
  * notes/3649 treats "ChangedEntitlement does not re-download" as the DESIRABLE
    behaviour that makes metadata-only edits cheap, and rejects a proposed patch
    on those grounds.

Same claim about firmware, opposite valence, and #3649 explicitly declined to
ship a change because of it.

IS EITHER OBSERVED? No. notes/3649's own "Verify plan" lists as step (3):

  "regression guard — edit a synced book's metadata only, sync, confirm it
   arrives as ChangedEntitlement and the device does NOT re-download. Needs
   cwn-local (currently Exited255) plus a Kobo client/emulator"

i.e. that note names it as a thing still to CONFIRM. It is an assumption in both
places, and it is honest about that in one of them.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE ORIGINAL FILING: a single unmeasured firmware
behaviour is currently deciding (a) whether the KEPUB repair reaches anyone, and
(b) whether #3649's format-conversion fix ships at all. One device experiment
settles both. That raises its value well above "tidy up a wrong comment".

THE EXPERIMENT, unchanged in shape but now worth more:
  1. a disposable, annotation-free book already synced to the device;
  2. record the on-device file's size/mtime/hash;
  3. bump only Books.last_modified server-side (no KoboSyncedBooks deletion);
  4. sync; re-measure.
Changed bytes => ChangedEntitlement re-delivers, and #3649's rejection of the
blunt patch loses its main argument. Unchanged => this finding's original claim
holds and the repair needs a different delivery mechanism.

Run the metadata-only arm from notes/3649's verify plan in the same sitting — it
is the same sync, read twice.

--- SCOPE CORRECTION, 2026-08-20: it decides THREE designs, not two ---

A third caller rests on the same unmeasured claim, found while verifying #1750's
wiring on merged main (F-fed247):

`cps/tasks/kepub_backfill.py` selects EVERY book in `KoboSyncedBooks` and hands
each to `TaskConvert`, whose split gate reduces to "the server holds no
annotations for this book". So the KEPUB backfill can split a book that has
already been on a Kobo.

Whether that can strand device-side highlights depends entirely on this
finding's open question:

  * device does NOT re-download on ChangedEntitlement -> the backfill is inert
    on already-synced devices and the gate is cosmetic;
  * device DOES re-download -> the EPUB->KEPUB format change is already
    disruptive for those books, and the split needs a gate that "no server
    annotations" cannot provide (37% of device bookmarks never reached the
    server, per F-a66189).

Same one sync. Three decisions.


---

UPDATE 2026-08-21 — this finding now has a MEASURED consequence on real hardware (F-2fcc0d).

Applying #1657's render predicate to all 30 annotations on the operator's own Clara BW
(fw 4.45.23792, read-only DB copy): 28 renderable, 2 NOT.

    The Able McLaughlins  dogear  ...#pgepubid00001
    The Age of Innocence  dogear  ...#pgepubid00008

Both carry a #fragment, so neither matches a ContentType=9 spine row and Nickel cannot render
them. The forward fix has shipped (#1773) -- these two are still broken because the books were
ALREADY DELIVERED before it, which is exactly the gap this finding names: the repair calls
mark_book_modified(..., unsync=False), so remove_synced_book never runs and the device is never
told to re-pull.

So the cost of leaving this open is no longer hypothetical: it is two of the operator's real
annotations, unrenderable on their own device, with no mechanism that will heal them.

Scope, honestly: both are DOGEARS. All 17 real highlights render. A lost dogear is a lost
place-marker, not lost user-authored text -- real, but smaller than 2-of-30 suggests.

ASSUMED, not observed: that re-delivery would actually fix them. Confirming it needs this
finding's own armed experiment plus a device sync, and a failed checkforchanges download makes
Nickel replace the local set with EMPTY -- unrecoverable, since KoboReader.sqlite is read-only
by standing rule.
title: KEPUB repair may never reach a device that already has the book, and two places document a mechanism the code does not implement
